subject: Modular entitlement packaging & channel netback for private offer
messages:
From: Lily Wong <lily.wong@zenithdata.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Modular entitlement packaging for private offer

Hi Vivek / Camila,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We are moving toward a private offer for a multi-cloud deployment (primarily Azure + GCP) and want to confirm how Redwood would package entitlements and what the channel economics look like. Attached is our PO requirements PDF. High-level asks: 

- Can Redwood map modular entitlements (core tokens / latency SLA add-on / dedicated KV cache) to separate SKUs suitable for a private offer?
- We need clarity on whether reseller netback is calculated off list price or net revenue after discounts/tax.
- Example workback showing final customer price for a 12-month commit (targets to follow) would be very helpful.
- Any constraints for invoice routing (Zenith directly vs. via reseller) and tax handling.

Timeline: procurement team aims to issue an LOI by Oct 6 if pricing and packaging match expectations.

Attaching: zenith_po_requirements.pdf

Can you confirm next steps and whether you need us to loop in our reseller partner?

Best,
Lily Wong
Head of Procurement, Zenith Data
procurement@zenithdata.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lily Wong <lily.wong@zenithdata.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Modular entitlement packaging for private offer

Hi Lily — thanks for the note and the attachment. We can absolutely support modular SKUs for private offers. A couple quick clarifying questions so our proposal aligns: 

1) Expected ARR / committed $ for 12 months (range is fine). That will drive tiering and any rebate thresholds.
2) Do you expect the reseller to invoice Zenith or to be a pass-through? If they invoice, we need reseller tax ID for routing.
3) Are there technical add-ons you want separately priced (e.g., dedicated KV cache, higher token SLA, managed on-prem connector)?

I will loop Camila (partner ops) and Irene (billing/procurement) to put together a compact workback and recommended channel netback ranges. If it helps, we can set a 30-min procurement alignment call next week.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of GTM — Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Lily Wong <lily.wong@zenithdata.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Modular entitlement packaging for private offer

Hi Lily — looping in a short proposal so you have something tangible for your LOI discussion. See attached spreadsheet for SKU mapping and sample price bands. Summary below: 

Modular packaging (recommended):
- SKU-RI-CORE: Base entitlements (token units, shared KV) — priced per 1M tokens/month
- SKU-RI-SLA: Low-latency SLA add-on (p99 latency, additional dedicated capacity) — monthly flat add-on
- SKU-RI-CACHE: Dedicated KV cache capacity (GB tiers) — monthly tiered pricing
- SKU-RI-EGRESS: Optional egress/data package for heavy export workloads

Channel netback (recommended ranges, US):
- Commit >= $1.2M/year: reseller netback 18% of list price
- Commit $400k–1.2M/year: reseller netback 14% of list price
- Commit < $400k/year: reseller netback 10% of list price

Notes:
- Our channel netback is structured off list price. Discounts in the private offer are applied before netback calculations; taxes are handled at invoice time and do not reduce the base netback percent (we pass tax through).
- If the reseller invoices Zenith directly, we can set the private offer price to list price and handle a downstream passback; otherwise Redwood can invoice Zenith and pay reseller via partner settlement.
- The attached cheatsheet (redwood_priv_offers_cheatsheet.xlsx) includes SKU IDs, example mapping to marketplace SKUs, and two conservative workbacks.

If this seems directionally OK, I can draft a DocuSign private offer and a short workback table for Zenith. Vivek — feel free to add billing/legal notes.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Sr. Partner Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
From: Lily Wong <lily.wong@zenithdata.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Modular entitlement packaging for private offer

Thanks Camila — that helps. A couple follow-ups: 

- When you say "netback is structured off list price" can you confirm whether that is gross list or the private-offer list (i.e., after our negotiated discount)? We want to ensure the reseller margin isn't unexpectedly eroded by deep private-offer discounts.
- For tax handling — can you confirm Redwood's preferred invoice flow for a US-headquartered customer with a US reseller?

Also — can you send a single-line workback example (final customer price per unit, Redwood revenue after netback, reseller margin) for one common config: CORE + SLA add-on for 1M tokens/month at the $400k/year commit level? We want to show this to finance.

Lily
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Lily Wong <lily.wong@zenithdata.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Modular entitlement packaging for private offer — sample workback

Hi Lily — quick inline workback for the CORE + SLA scenario at the $400k/year commit band. Numbers are illustrative but use the recommended netback range.

Example workback (annualized):
- List price (annualized for the SKU bundle): $500,000
- Private-offer negotiated discount to Zenith: 20% -> Net customer price: $400,000
- Reseller netback (14% of list price per Camila's banding): 14% x $500,000 = $70,000
- Redwood recognized revenue (net of reseller settlement): Net customer price - reseller settlement = $400,000 - $70,000 = $330,000
- Tax handling: Sales tax is added on invoice; Redwood does not net tax against revenue recognized. If reseller invoices Zenith, reseller is responsible for collecting/filing; otherwise Redwood will collect tax.

Notes / options:
- If you prefer netback calculated off net customer price instead of list, we can model that; it typically reduces Redwood's effective revenue by ~10–15% on similar deals.
- Invoice routing recommendation: For clarity and faster procurement, have Zenith accept Redwood invoice directly for the Private Offer and add reseller on settlement. This avoids invoice disputes and short-pay situations.

I've created a draft private-offer DocuSign and linked it here for visibility: https://www.docusign.com/partner/ZN-1187-draft
Also adding the HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/6789012

If this aligns, we can schedule a short procurement call (Irene, Camila, Vivek + Lily + ClearBridge) to finalize SKU list and DocuSign.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
